question: Does the complete identity-proved target-and-death trace contain a reliable, viable, policy-selective and functionally separated natural capacity for a deliberate change between the first two single-target Attacks in one player turn while the first target remains alive?
hypothesis: Runtime target selection is a narrower policy decision than owning or playing two single-target Attacks: the death-disambiguated first-pair predicate should retain robust active and exact-inactive policy sets, broad exact-card support, both target-transition directions and separation from the closed Scoreline and Afterimage opportunity sets.

closedFamilyExclusions.namedCardSequencing: Scoreline, Afterimage, their timing controls and commitment fallbacks remain closed. Exact card IDs are breadth witnesses only.
closedFamilyExclusions.genericCadence: The closed cadence family alternates Attack and Skill over three plays. This audit uses exactly the first two authored single-target Attacks and estimates no cadence payoff.
closedFamilyExclusions.focusedToSweep: The closed fanout family changes authored scope from enemy to allEnemies. Both target-transfer cards have authored target=enemy and differ only by runtime living target index.
closedFamilyExclusions.shatterFacetAndStatus: No HIT, CHIP, SHATTER, Facet, damage or status event enters the predicate. DIE is used only to reject a forced target change.
closedFamilyExclusions.otherClosedFamilies: Do not reconstruct Kindle, Ward, Ember-reserve damage, relic, one-bit setup, action-economy, weak-mend, same-instance repeat, acquisition scalar or private-debt paths.
closedFamilyExclusions.method: No ML, RL, optimiser, policy remap, grammar expansion or adaptive candidate tuning is permitted.

mechanismContract.researchIdentity: dusk-target-transfer; a research identity, not shipping copy.
mechanismContract.producer: After an exact Duskblade Attack with authored target=enemy resolves while combat remains live and its selected target remains alive, store that target index.
mechanismContract.mediatorState: One player-combat previous-target integer plus one paid Boolean for the current player turn; neither is a RunState or save field.
mechanismContract.consumer: The next exact Attack in the same player turn with authored target=enemy consumes the mediator only when it selects a different living enemy index after its unchanged authored effects and while combat remains live.
mechanismContract.payoffOperation: After valid consumption, request exactly one Ember through the existing bounded Ember operation, at most once in that player turn; requested and realised values remain separate telemetry.
mechanismContract.lifecycle: The previous-target mediator and paid flag clear at each player-turn start and combat end. Other card types and all-enemy Attacks neither consume nor replace it. A same-target Attack replaces the stored index without paying. Target death clears the stored index before another single-target Attack can consume it.
mechanismContract.naturalCost: Enter a multi-enemy fight, draw and pay for at least two existing single-target Attacks in one turn, keep the first target alive, then select a different living target for the next single-target Attack.
mechanismContract.acquisition: None. Existing current-main reward pools, rarities, cards and deck/save representation remain unchanged.
mechanismContract.duskBoundary: The existing Emberheart is the proposed Dusk gate. Ashwarden and mechanism-off are exact current-main paths; Emberheart's authored post-combat healing is unchanged.
mechanismContract.factorIsolation: Scoreline and Afterimage are separate factors fixed off. Target transfer reads only card type, authored target scope, exact selected target index, target death, current turn and exact Emberheart identity.
mechanismContract.rngAndPersistence: No RNG call or cursor movement, no new run-persistent field, internal ID, save version, content entry, reward entry or acquisition UI.
mechanismContract.telemetry: Direct research-only producer, target-survived, mediator-set/replacement/clear, consumer, same-target rejection, forced-death rejection, mediator-consume, payoff and turn-expiry stages with exact card and target indices plus requested and realised Ember.

targetSwitchPayoff.definition: Dusk-only target-transfer mediator and one-Ember payoff defined by the complete mechanism contract.
targetSwitchPayoff.status: Fixed off here. The enabled level does not exist and may be implemented only after capacity success in a separate exact-null and direct-mediator identity stage.

scorelinePayoff.definition: Separate closed causal factor fixed absent and never pooled with the target-transfer endpoint.

afterimagePayoff.definition: Separate closed causal factor fixed absent and never pooled with the target-transfer endpoint.

acquisitionPriority.definition: Frozen exact reward policy; not varied or estimated.

frozenCausalFactors.independence: All causal factors are fixed off. This is not the old four-factor design and contains no causal or joint package cell.

identity-proved-current-main-trace.status: Immutable cached observation arm only; deterministic reconstruction adds no simulator row.

design.type: zero-new-row complete-cohort actual-switch capacity and alias audit; not a factorial and not a causal experiment
design.construction: In every eligible player turn, filter plays to authored type=attack,target=enemy and classify only the first two. A deliberate switch requires differing target indices and no DIE for the first target strictly between the two PLAY events.
design.fightRule: Only fights whose frozen starting formation has at least two enemies are eligible. At most the first filtered pair per player turn is counted; intervening other card types and target scopes do not reset or consume the observation interval.
mechanisticallyJustifiedInteractions: First PLAY target index by intervening DIE index by second PLAY target index defines deliberate switching; none alone is sufficient.
Multi-enemy starting formation by two-single-target-Attack context is structural eligibility, not an estimated product interaction.
Dusk/Emberheart identity by target-switch payoff is the sole future causal interaction and is not estimated here.
design.aliasStructure: A differing target index without DIE exclusion aliases forced change after target death. Same-target pairs are explicit non-activations. Robust upper-bound-context policies without robust deliberate switches reject two-Attack opportunity as sufficient. Exact card IDs and ordered target-index transitions are breadth witnesses, not candidate cells. Forced-death-only and same-target policy sets are descriptive alias controls, not extra candidate levels or post-look rescue gates.
design.interference: Scoreline and Afterimage remain separate and fixed off. Their immutable robust opportunity sets are shared repertoire-overlap anchors only. No joint cell has decision value before target-transfer identity and a later comparable CRN effect establish an independently admitted package.
design.omittedCells: No exact-target-specific candidate, reverse direction, adjacency variant, third-Attack rescue, exact-card subset, payoff value, acquisition, rarity, policy knob, Ash intervention, RandomBuild, simulator, held-out, joint-package, ML, RL, optimiser or protected-seed cell is authorised.

sourceAnchors.meaning: Complete current-main authored type=attack,target=enemy inventory. Observed exact IDs are breadth witnesses only.

trace.selectionRule: Read all 256 rows of the sole identity-proved target/death observation output. No row, policy, seed, fight, turn, pair or endpoint is selected after observation.

cohort.identity: Every policy and seed from the complete frozen current-main rectangle is read exactly once; each policy has one exact frozen snapshot across its four seeds.

upperBoundContext.definition: A robust policy reaches at least one first-two-single-target-Attack turn in at least two of four frozen rows.
upperBoundContext.status: Immutable cross-stage consistency anchor from the prior observation-eligibility result.

scoreline.definition: A robust policy plays Chisel before a later Executioner in one fight in at least two of four frozen rows.
scoreline.status: Immutable overlap anchor only; Scoreline remains closed and fixed off.

afterimage.definition: A robust policy simultaneously holds Ward and Warden's Edge in at least two of four frozen rows.
afterimage.status: Immutable conservative overlap anchor only; Afterimage remains closed and fixed off.

estimands.unit: Policy identity over its complete four-seed rectangle.
estimands.active: At least one deliberate first-pair target switch in at least two of four rows.
estimands.inactive: No deliberate first-pair target switch in any of four rows.
estimands.viable: An active policy with at least one qualifying row that wins.
estimands.contextOnly: Robust upper-bound-context policies minus robust deliberate-switch policies.
estimands.targetChangeIgnoringDeath: Robust policies with differing first-pair target indices before applying the death exclusion; descriptive only.
estimands.deathAliasOnly: Robust target-index-change policies minus robust deliberate-switch policies; descriptive evidence of the targetIdx-only alias, not a success gate.
estimands.sameTarget: Robust policies with a first-pair same-target observation; descriptive non-activation evidence, not a success gate.
estimands.breadth: Distinct exact first cards, second cards, ordered card pairs and ordered target-index transitions over deliberate-switch turns.
estimands.separation: Candidate-only, anchor-only, cross-active and Jaccard policy-set overlap against the separate Scoreline and Afterimage anchors.
estimands.reliability: Pre-existing stall/error rows and impossible dead-target reuse in the immutable trace; no added-fault estimand exists because no simulator runs.
estimands.notEstimated: Gameplay mediator identity, Ember payoff, causal complementarity, duration effect, Ash isolation, RandomBuild/global-power movement, held-out reproducibility, package admission, detector score, product balance or protected confirmation.

gates.provenance: The 16-policy active/inactive, eight-policy viability, package-separation, 0.55 overlap and one immutable baseline-fault limits reuse the frozen 64-policy structural-capacity scale. Eight context-only policies require the runtime choice to add information beyond two-Attack opportunity. Four cards per position and eight ordered pairs reject a named-card alias. Two ordered target transitions reject a fixed-index-direction alias. Forced-death and same-target controls remain descriptive because their absence cannot invalidate the conservative survival predicate and they are not candidate cells.

claimBoundary: Natural policy capacity, runtime-choice selectivity and closed-package repertoire separation only; no gameplay implementation, mediator identity, Ember payoff, causal, package-admission, detector, product or P9 claim.

decisionRules.success: Every immutable, source, trace, policy-identity, active, inactive, viability, context-only, exact-card breadth, target-transition breadth, package-separation, semantic-validity, reliability, budget and zero-ledger check passes at the sole complete look.
decisionRules.successAuthority: Apply boundary 1: freeze only the exact dusk-target-transfer contract for a separately preregistered exact-null and direct-mediator identity prototype. Do not vary pair position, target direction, card identity, payoff, carrier, acquisition or policy, and do not add a causal simulator row before omitted/off identity and direct producer, same-target, target-death, consumer, once-per-turn and scope-isolation controls pass.
decisionRules.futility: Any declared active, inactive, viability, context-only, breadth, transition, separation, semantic-validity or reliability gate fails on the complete immutable trace.
decisionRules.futilityAuthority: Apply boundary 2: close the exact target-transfer family without third-Attack, adjacency, target-direction, card-subset, payoff, carrier, cohort, policy or method rescue and continue with the next evidence-backed minimal structural mechanism inside #421.
decisionRules.inconclusive: An immutable input, source, trace, schema, policy identity, ledger or wall-time check prevents the complete deterministic decision.
decisionRules.inconclusiveAuthority: Apply boundary 3: record the exact missing relevant gate at the frozen cap; add no repair, rerun, replacement trace, simulator row, method or protected seed, then follow the current human-authority contract for an unavailable or inconclusive relevant gate.

order: Verify live task, current-main instructions, repository/archive refs, closed-family evidence, source, task capsule, helpers, trace identity and ledger identities.
Reconstruct and classify only the first two single-target Attacks in every player turn of every frozen multi-enemy fight.
Apply support, inactivity, viability, context-only, breadth, transition, package-separation, semantic-validity and reliability gates once.
Verify the ledger is byte-identical and apply exactly one decision boundary.
executionAndStopping.firstLook: The complete 256-row cached rectangle is the sole look. No predicate, pair position, threshold, cohort, anchor or endpoint may change after execution begins.
executionAndStopping.stagedConstraint: This stage can reject or justify one exact-null and direct-mediator identity prototype only. It contains no intervention or comparably evaluated enabled endpoint and cannot support a causal or package claim.
executionAndStopping.futureCrnConstraint: Any later causal contrast must use the same frozen policy identities, simulation seed identities, baseline, first-look budget, estimator and stopping rule at every compared level. Cheap path evidence may precede whole-run evidence but cannot support an endpoint not comparably evaluated.
executionAndStopping.knobIdentityConstraint: Before any future mechanism row, omitted and explicit-off settings must reproduce exact path, RNG identity and result, and deterministic direct controls must prove the knob affects only the target-transfer mediator and declared bounded payoff.
executionAndStopping.methodConstraint: Deterministic code owns construction, caching, fitting and stop/go. No ML, RL or optimiser is authorised unless a later comparable experiment isolates a remaining policy-repertoire bottleneck and measures decision value for the added method.
executionAndStopping.stopping: One zero-row complete-cohort look; exactly one of success, futility or inconclusive is recorded. No sequential peeking, third-card rescue, target-direction split, subset selection, threshold relaxation, cohort replacement or endpoint addition.
